amendments.what: NC1 was specified as a within-protein permutation required to cover 0.5. The first run returned 0.5168 [0.5055, 0.5280] in the label-negative stratum, i.e. a failure under the literal text. Diagnosis: the statistic pools across proteins, so a within-protein permutation is not a null for it -- it leaves the between-protein alignment intact. The control was mis-specified, not the estimator.
amendments.fix: Split into NC1a (GLOBAL permutation, a true null, GATING, must cover 0.5) and NC1b (within-protein permutation, reported as the between-protein floor, not gating).
what_this_amendment_does_NOT_change: the primary quantity, the branches E1-E4 and the verdict rule are untouched
nothing was relaxed: the gating control is now a strictly correct null, where the original was not a null at all
the failing number is kept and reported as NC1b, because it is informative

manuscript_defect_found.what: Figure F3 panel a's caption says the panel shows the AUC against the distal (6-12-residue) trypsin cleavage band. The plotting script reads results/self_audit_cleavage_flank.csv, i.e. the kr_sfe006_offsets attribute (K or R at offsets -10,-8,-7,-6,-4,-2,4,5,6,7,8). The body's 0.6415 / 0.6298 match that table, so text and figure agree with each other and with the data; the CAPTION names the wrong attribute. The distal band's stored values for the same model are 0.6570 / 0.5956.
manuscript_defect_found.severity: must: a reader recomputing the distal band would not obtain the quoted numbers

what_this_does_NOT_establish: it does not make 3.3 or 3.4 public; those need refitting
it does not say whether the model is a good persulfidation predictor
both cohorts are persulfidation; nothing transfers to other chemistries
scores are full-fit on external cohorts, so an absence of association could also mean poor transfer rather than absence of bias
